title: BLS glossary: earnings, wages and salaries, employed persons
author: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics
citation: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Glossary (bls.gov/opub/hom/glossary.htm)
difficulty: in our words; not read to children
why: Earnings are pay for work over a period of time; wages are counted by the hour; being employed means paid work, and the survey definition leaves out volunteer work and work around one's own home
note: page read 2026-11-20: earnings are "Remuneration (pay, wages) of a worker or group of workers for services performed during a specific period of time"; the wage rate is the straight-time hourly rate or, for workers not paid hourly, earnings divided by hours; employed persons did at least one hour of paid work (or worked in their own business), and volunteer work and work around one's own home do not count for the survey. Our grade 1 meaning is simpler: employed = has a job where someone pays you; income = money received for work; wages = pay counted by the hour. We say that unpaid work is still work. Government surveys also count people who run their own business as employed; grade 1 says only that Hal and Mara earn by selling what they make. A U.S. government page; no licence stated.
